preview_en:
After spending the week at the bottom of Ligue 1, Nice face the difficult task of digging themselves out of their early-season hole against pre-round table-toppers Lille .

Match News and Current Form

Nice’s winless start to the season was extended to four games after a 1-0 loss to Auxerre (D2, L2), with that being the fourth time in their last five Ligue 1 games they failed to score. That streak embodies how the Eagles have had their wings clipped this year, having picked up just 17 points in Ligue 1 in 2026, the fewest of any current Ligue 1 club across that period. Their home form has especially let them down over the last ten months with no wins in their last 13 home league games (excluding the relegation play-off), with nine of those being drawn, the most home draws of any team in the big-five European leagues this calendar year.

Lille have begun their domestic season in scintillating form, making it three wins from their four league games with a 2-0 win over Troyes last round, with the other result being a frustrating 2-2 draw with PSG in which they led 2-0 going into stoppage time. Keeping clean sheets in three of those matches means the Mastiffs have conceded just 19 Ligue 1 goals this year, fewer than any other current Ligue 1 side, allowing new manager Davide Ancelotti to potentially make history here with Lille as with eight away league victories in a row, he could now see Lille equal the longest winning away streak in the top-flight, set by Marseille between February and August 2009.

Head-to-Head History

Nice have lost just one of the last eight H2Hs (W3, D4) and have proven to be even more dominant at the Allianz Riviera, suffering just one defeat in their last 14 home encounters with Lille (W6, D7).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Only one of Nice's last five league games saw both teams score.

Nice have scored just one first-half goal in their last seven home Ligue 1 matches.

Just one of Lille’s last six league games saw both teams score.

Lille haven't won the corner count in any of their last five outings.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Nice’s Isak Jansson might earn his first start of the season since four of his last five goals have come at home, the most recent being in this fixture last season. Lille’s Ethan Mbappé sealed the points against Troyes with a stoppage-time goal, that being the third of his last four strikes to come after the 80th minute.

Antoine Mendy and Laurent Abergel both missed Nice’s last match, while Lille’s only absentee is Hamza Igamane .
